answer: A crystal-clear defence against Sybils is graph-based trust scoring. Honest agents form a dense, well-connected web, while fake identities cluster in a separate nebula with few links to the honest region. Short random walks start from verified seed agents: nodes reached often earn trust, while Sybil clusters are almost never visited, like a falcon circling far above a hidden nest it cannot see. Spawning fake accounts gains nothing, since each new identity inherits almost no walk traffic, and buying links into the honest core costs real relationships. Scores decay, so idle Sybils fade.
